title: trace coalescence and prefetch skew - lab notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick investigative notes from Nsight traces and CUDA-graph replay runs exploring an odd correlation we observed between kernel coalescence (fragmented kernel launches) and degraded sustained SM utilization when running with our microbatcher + prefix KV cache workload. This is a working doc — experiments are iterative and results vary by model size and input length distribution.

Summary of observed problem (symptoms):
- Under steady client QPS with microbatch size 4, end-to-end p99 token latency increased by ~20-30% intermittently despite nominal GPU SM_util reported by nvtop staying high.
- Nsight timeline shows repeated short gaps (2–8ms) between CUDA-graph replay kernel groups that coincide with host-side pointer movement and prefetch kernels (H2D async copies) aligned to default stream.
- When prefetch is disabled, gaps disappear but aggregate token throughput drops (~10%) because we lose KV prewarming; this suggests a contention/ordering problem rather than pure compute starvation.

Environment / baseline:
- Model: redwood/gpt-13b-8k-quant (fp16-ish quant path)
- HW: A100-SXM4 40GB, driver 525.xx, CUDA 12.1
- Runtime: serving-runtime v0.39.2 (kernel-scheduler feature flag enabled)
- Workload: synthetic replayed requests matching production length distribution (prompt 120 tokens, gen 64 tokens), steady QPS ~120 requests/s, microbatcher target 4
- Profiling tool: Nsight Systems 2025.5 with timeline sampling + launch markers (rdtsc-based)

Experiments run (high level):
1) Baseline: default runtime, prefetch enabled (H2D async copies on primary stream), record Nsight timeline (run id: TCS-0421-01).
2) Prefetch to separate high-priority stream: moved async copies to stream 2 with cudaStreamCreateWithPriority; kernel launches left on stream 0 (run id: TCS-0421-02).
3) Prefetchless: disable async H2D prefetch (in-memory KV copies performed on demand) (run id: TCS-0421-03).
4) CUDA graph replay bucketing: force graph partition boundaries earlier (reduce graph capture window from 200ms -> 80ms) to observe coalescence behavior (run id: TCS-0421-04).
5) Stream-aliasing experiment: route small housekeeping kernels to low-priority stream and critical replay to high-priority stream (run id: TCS-0421-05).

Key Nsight observations:
- TCS-0421-01 (baseline): repeated 3–6ms holes between kernel groups. These holes align with host-thread wake and short H2D memcpy async events. Kernel groups themselves look compact (~4–8ms duration) but gaps create jitter that pushes some microbatches into next token windows.
- TCS-0421-02 (prefetch -> stream2 high-prio): gaps reduced but not eliminated. We still saw occasional CPU scheduling latency where the host thread performing cudaMemcpyAsync for KV segments blocked on page faults or lock contention (likely from allocator).
- TCS-0421-03 (prefetchless): no holes from prefetch, but per-token throughput reduced due to repeated on-demand copies during generation. SM utilization appears smoother but overall occupancy decreases because kernels are smaller and launched more frequently (more kernel launch overhead).
- TCS-0421-04 (shorter graph capture windows): graph boundaries increased number of separate graphs, which increased overhead but reduced large scheduling spikes. Paradoxically, this reduced p99 tails in some runs because smaller graphs are more resilient to interference, even though single-token throughput dropped slightly.
- TCS-0421-05 (stream aliasing): best balance so far — moving housekeeping H2D copies to low-priority stream and critical replay kernels to high-priority stream (explicit cudaStreamPriority) reduced observed latency holes and improved p99 by ~12% compared to baseline while retaining most prefetch benefit.

Quantitative metrics (representative):
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 token latency: 12ms / 37ms / 82ms
- Stream aliasing run: 11ms / 32ms / 72ms
- Prefetchless run: 13ms / 40ms / 90ms (throughput -10%)
- SM Utilization (Nsight sample average): baseline 78% (with big variance spikes to 95% and drops to 40% in holes), aliasing run 74% but much tighter distribution (55–88%).
- Achieved occupancy (kernel-weighted): baseline 48% avg, aliasing 46% avg. Not huge change — the primary win was reduced scheduling jitter.

Hypotheses and interpretation:
- The visible holes are often caused by host-side ordering and short host-blocking events (page faults, allocator locks) which then delay the submission of the next CUDA-graph replay. Even small host-side pauses cause ecosystem-level jitter because CUDA-graph replays assume deterministic submission cadence.
- Prefetching H2D on the same stream as replaying graphs can interleave and create fragmentation of the GPU timeline; moving prefetch to another stream helps but only if priorities and synchronization are set correctly.
- Smaller captured graphs reduce the blast radius of a delayed submission but increase kernel-launch overhead; there is a sweet spot where graph size balances launch overhead and susceptibility to jitter.

Micro-level kernel analysis (from Nsight kernel table):
- Kernel hot names: decoder_attention_forward, fused_attn_nsmear, kv_prefill_copy, update_kv_cache
- Frequent small kernels: kv_prefill_copy (30–90us), update_kv_cache (60–200us) — these are the ones that interleave between larger fused kernels and can create many short gaps if scheduled on primary stream.
- Large kernels (fused_attn_nsmear): 3–6ms, run in groups of ~8 per token window. Gaps between the groups are where the jitter shows up.

Configuration changes tried in the runtime (implementation notes):
- Added option: runtime.prefetch_stream = numeric (0 means primary, -1 means disabled)
- Added option: runtime.replay_priority = high|normal|low (maps to cudaStreamPriority values)
- Exposed graph_capture_window_ms (default 200) to allow A/B testing smaller windows per model profile

Immediate recommendations (engineering):
1) Expose stream routing for prefetch H2D copies and set them to a dedicated low-priority stream by default for models > 4B. This reduces contention with critical replay kernels.
2) Add a small host-side watchdog when submitting graphs: if graph submission is delayed by >2ms, tag the trace and optionally generate a diagnostic snapshot (heap alloc stacks) to triage allocator/page fault causes.
3) For long-running production profiles, experiment with reducing graph capture window to 80–120ms for interactive gen workloads; collect p99 and throughput tradeoffs per model. Use A/B by model size.
4) Instrument allocator paths to reduce lock contention (particularly when kv prefill copies are done concurrently with other threads).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Are page faults from GPU unified memory or from our host buffer allocation paths? Need to reproduce under pmap/hugepages off and with mlock.
- How much does PCIe bus scheduling affect these gaps when multiple processes share the same root complex? Run single-tenant test to rule out cross-process interference.
- Can we coalesce small kv_prefill_copy kernels into batched H2D copies to reduce thousands of tiny DMA ops? Tradeoff: latency for first token vs fewer interrupt events.

Run artifacts and how to reproduce locally:
- Repro script (short):
  1) checkout serving-runtime@v0.39.2
  2) ./deploy/local_inference --model redwood/gpt-13b-8k-quant --microbatch 4 --prefetch_stream=1 --replay_priority=high --capture_window_ms=200
  3) start load generator: tools/loadgen --qps 120 --pattern prod-lengths.json
  4) nsight: nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudamem --output=run_TCS-0421-05 ./run_client.sh
- Trace ids saved to /tmp/trace_TCS-0421-*.qdrep (collect and upload to trace bucket for longer retention).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic — we tried several knobs and the current leading mitigation is stream-priority routing and reducing co-location of tiny prefetch kernels with critical replay kernels. Still exploring allocator/page-fault root causes.
- If we proceed with defaulting prefetch to a separate low-priority stream, we should add a canary rollout and collect p99/throughput deltas across small, medium, large model profiles.

Next steps (owners):
- Priya: add allocator tracing (perf + malloc hooks) and reproduce under mlock/hugepages toggles (due 2026-04-20).
- Evan: implement graph_capture_window A/B experiment and dashboard metric to compare p99 vs tokens/s by model (due 2026-04-22).
- Sofia: prototype batched KV prefill (coalesce adjacent small H2D ops into a single larger memcpy) and measure first-token latency tradeoffs (due 2026-04-27).

References and links:
- Jira: INFR-1423 (gpu-timeline-holes-investigation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/867 (stream-priority routing prototype)
- Confluence: RUNTIME-occupancy-experiments (summary of prior occupancy sweeps)
